name: Bánh căn
summary: A rice cake cooked in a clay mold with no oil. The provincial digital guide puts a quail egg, fresh squid, or a whole shrimp on the batter, and names it at the Trần Phú night market and along Tháp Bà in the late afternoon.
origin: Nha Trang. The night market is behind 46 Trần Phú. A street-snack article also puts sidewalk stalls along Tháp Bà in the late afternoon, and names the Phan Rang market as a second place.
texture: The provincial digital guide says the batter is rice soaked overnight, milled fine, and poured thin into a hot clay mold. No oil. The cake stays dry, with a light charred smell.
taste: The provincial digital guide’s words for a bite are a crisp shell, sweet seafood, and a béo bùi xíu mại.
howToEat: The bánh căn article names three dips: sweet-sour fish sauce, mắm nêm, or salty-sweet nước mắm cá kho. Each bowl gets scallion oil, pork xíu mại, and chopped mango.

A street-snack article on the same site says the coastal cake, unlike Đà Lạt bánh căn eaten with xíu mại broth, is dipped in sweet-sour fish sauce, nước cá kho tót, and scallion oil. Both accounts stay.
Plates named on the bánh căn article: chicken or quail egg, mực lá, shrimp, and minced beef, plus fried shallot and scallion oil. They are toppings of this cake.
where: The 137 m walking street behind 46 Trần Phú, Lộc Thọ, with bún chả and chả cá. A stall number was not printed.
Late afternoon along Tháp Bà. The same article names the Phan Rang market. That is not a Nha Trang address.
seoTitle: Bánh căn in Nha Trang — the clay-mold cake
seoDescription: What the provincial digital guide puts on a Nha Trang bánh căn: squid, shrimp, or egg, in a clay mold, at the night market and along Tháp Bà.
